snapshot.title: TNPSC Economy: Agri, Industry & Services
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Economy Hook: Agri: Swaminathan. Services: Top GDP. RBI: 1935. 1969: Nationalization. Disguised: Agri. MSME: Jobs.

quick_notes.title: Agriculture (Primary Sector)
quick_notes.detail: Green Revolution (1960s - M.S. Swaminathan). Major crops : Paddy, Wheat. Subsidy types : Fertilizer, Power.
quick_notes.explanation: Agricultureis part of the primary sector, which means it involves growing crops and raising animals directly from the land. The Green Revolution was a period in the 1960s when scientist M.S. Swaminathan helped increase food production in India using high-yield seeds and modern methods. The major

quick_notes.title: Industry (Secondary Sector)
quick_notes.detail: Navratna, Maharatna, Miniratna status for PSUs. MSME (Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises) - vital for employment in TN.
quick_notes.explanation: The secondary sector involves industries that transform raw materials into finished goods. Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) are government-owned companies that receive special classifications like Maharatna, Navratna, or Miniratna based on their size and profitability; these statuses grant them greater financial and operational independence. For example, Maharatna status is given to the largest and most profitable PSUs, Navratna to medium-sized ones, and Miniratna to smaller PSUs. MSME stands for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises, which are businesses defined by their lower investment in equipment or number of employees. In Tamil Nadu, MSMEs are vital because they generate a large share of employment and support the state's economy.

quick_notes.title: Services (Tertiary Sector)
quick_notes.detail: Largest contributor to GDP (~54%). Banking, IT, Tourism, Insurance.
quick_notes.explanation: The tertiary sector, also called the service sector, is the part of the economy that provides services rather than producing goods. Examples include banking, information technology (IT), tourism, and insurance. GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, which is the total value of all goods and services produced in a country in a year. In India, the tertiary sector is the largest contributor to GDP, accounting for about 54 percent of the total. This means that more than half of India's economic output comes from services like those listed above.

quick_notes.title: Unemployment Types
quick_notes.detail: Disguised (Agri), Seasonal, Structural, Frictional. TN has various schemes for skill development (Naan Mudhalvan).
quick_notes.explanation: Unemployment has four main types. Disguised unemployment happens when more people work on a farm than needed, such as in agriculture (farming), so some workers add no real output. Seasonal unemployment occurs when jobs only exist during certain times of the year, like harvesting. Structural unemployment arises when workers' skills do not match available jobs due to changes in the economy. Frictional unemployment is the short period between leaving one job and finding another. Tamil Nadu (TN) runs skill development programs, such as Naan Mudhalvan, which is a government scheme that trains people in new skills to help them get jobs.

quick_notes.title: Banking & RBI
quick_notes.detail: RBI (Established 1935, Nationalized 1949). Monetary Policy (Repo, Reverse Repo). Banks Nationalization (1969 - 14 banks).
quick_notes.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India, or RBI, is the central bank of India, which means it is the main bank that controls all other banks and the country's money supply. It was first set up in 1935 as a private company, but the government took full control of it in 1949, a process called nationalization. One of the RBI's most important jobs is to manage Monetary Policy, which is the set of actions it takes to control the amount of money in the economy and keep prices stable. To do this, it uses tools like the Repo Rate, which is the interest rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks, and the Reverse Repo Rate, which is the interest rate the RBI pays to banks when they deposit extra money with it. In 1969, the government nationalized 14 large private banks, meaning it took ownership of them to make banking services more widely available to the public, especially in rural areas.
